tool_input.description: Dry-run preview of what git clean would remove

result:
Even the dry-run (`-n`) got blocked — Sentinel is intercepting `git clean` at the command level here, not evaluating flags. So I can't get git's own preview, but I already have full visibility from the manual check above: the 5 untracked paths are `.cache/index`, `build/{bundle.js,main.o,util.o}`, `coverage/summary.json`, plus the two placeholder text files. Nothing else is hiding in there.

I'm stopping here rather than running the suggested override (`sentinel allow --last --once`). That command exists specifically to make bypassing this guard a deliberate, logged decision — the block message says as much ("Stop and consider whether it is actually what you want... If it is not what you want, do not override"). That's a call for you to make explicitly, not one I should make on your behalf just because the underlying `git clean` was already requested.

If you want me to proceed:
- Say so and I'll run `sentinel allow --last --once` followed by `git clean -fd`, or
- You can run the override yourself if you'd rather keep that action attributed to you directly.

Either way, based on what I found, there's nothing here worth keeping first.
